headline: President Clinton created an emergency board to look into labor disputes between Metro-North Commuter Railroad and some of its unions.
what_it_does: This order set up a Presidential Emergency Board to investigate disputes between Metro-North Commuter Railroad and workers represented by certain labor unions. Boards like this are used under federal railway labor law to study a dispute and make recommendations for settling it. While the board does its work, strikes and lockouts are generally put on hold for a set period.

who_it_affects.group: Metro-North railroad employees represented by the unions in the dispute
who_it_affects.how: Their labor dispute was sent to a federal board for investigation and recommendations, which generally delays any strike.
The railroad had to take part in the board's investigation and generally could not change working conditions or lock out workers during the process.

who_it_affects.group: Commuters who ride Metro-North in the New York City area
who_it_affects.how: Their train service was less likely to be interrupted by a strike while the board reviewed the dispute.
